payload.summary: Added the pure chooseAccount/switchReason account policy on top of decide, optional `account` on the four session/usage/limit events, and the new account.switched event, with tests.
payload.commitMessage: feat(limits): add account choice policy and account events
notes: src/limits/policy.ts: exported types AccountUsage { name; limits: AccountLimits; snapshot: UsageSnapshot | null; blockedUntil: Date | null }, AccountChoice (go{account} | wait{account, until, reason: 'session-low'|'limit-hit'} | stop{reason:'weekly-low', resetsAt}), SwitchReason

chooseAccount(accounts, { burn, current }, now): AccountChoice — throws plain Error on empty list; candidate order = current (if in list) then list order; per account: weekly-low skip → blockedUntil > now wait limit-hit (until = blockedUntil as given, no margin added) → decide wait session-low → go
Without burn the first non-weekly-low candidate decides; with burn first go wins, else earliest until (ties to earlier candidate); all weekly-low → stop with earliest non-null weekly resetsAt
A weekly-low account is skipped even when it is also blocked (weekly checked first)
switchReason(from, now): 'limit-hit' if blocked, else 'weekly-low'/'session-low' by decide, else 'priority'
decide() unchanged (already took AccountLimits since MA-1)

src/events/eventSchema.ts: optional `account: string` on usage.snapshot, limit.wait, session.started, session.finished (missing = default); new AccountSwitchedSchema t:'account.switched' {task, from, to, reason} in EventSchema; exported ACCOUNT_SWITCH_REASONS
src/events/taskState.ts needed no change: account.switched has a task but falls into the default branch

payload.summary: The runner now takes a list of accounts. Before every segment it refreshes each account's usage, picks one with chooseAccount (sticky within a task, --burn and weekly-low skipping) and runs the segment with that account's env. It writes `account` on its events and appends account.switched on a switch; a single default account behaves as before.
payload.commitMessage: feat(runner): choose and switch between Claude accounts per segment
notes: src/runner/runSpec.ts: export type RunAccount = PreparedAccount & { probe: () => Promise<UsageSnapshot | null> }; RunSpecDeps.probeUsage replaced by accounts: readonly [RunAccount, ...RunAccount[]] (priority order)
RunSpecOptions.burn?: boolean (optional, default false); RunAllOptions.burn?: boolean, forwarded to runSpec only when set
Per-run state in runSpec: snapshots Map, blockedUntil Map, probeFailing Set, lastAccount (initialised to accounts[0].name, so leaving the priority account on the first segment emits account.switched)
pauseCheck(task, current) probes every stale account (one reporter.phase 'usage' per probe), then chooseAccount; a wait clears that account's snapshot and block
limit outcome: blockedUntil set (limitHitTarget/waitTarget as before), chooseAccount(current = segment account) without probing; wait → wait + clear; stop → paused-weekly; then limit-resume
account written on session.started, session.finished, usage.snapshot, limit.wait; account.switched {task, from, to, reason: switchReason(from)}
paused-weekly message: 'weekly usage left below the minimum' (1 account) / '... on every account' (several); probe warning gets ' for <name>' only with several accounts

Test harness: runSpec.spec.ts start() accepts accounts?: [RunAccount, ...]; default builds 'default' from probeUsage/probes; runAll.spec.ts deps() uses a default account with a null probe
docs/v1/README.md: SRD-38 Accounts row added; SRD-10 ends with '(several accounts: SRD-38)'

deviations.what: `burn` is optional (`burn?: boolean`, default false) on RunSpecOptions and RunAllOptions, not a required boolean. run.ts doesn't pass `burn: false` explicitly.
deviations.why: A required field would change existing assertions. run.spec.ts compares the runSpec options and runAll options with toEqual, and runAll.spec.ts calls runAll without burn. The spec rules forbid changing what existing cases assert.

deviations.what: lastAccount starts as the priority account, so a first segment on the fallback emits account.switched from the priority account.
deviations.why: The Done-when cases expect account.switched (weekly-low / session-low) on the run's very first task. Without an initial lastAccount, the first segment has no previous account to switch from.

question.text: Should the first segment of a run emit account.switched when it doesn't run on the priority account?
options: Yes: lastAccount starts as the priority account
No: lastAccount starts as null and the first segment never emits a switch
question.chosen: Yes: lastAccount starts as the priority account

deviations.what: Added two cases the brief doesn't list: a per-account probe-warning case, and a case where the next task stays on the fallback while the priority account is still blocked. The runAll.spec.ts harness now builds a default account instead of probeUsage.
deviations.why: These cover the new warning text and the sticky/blocked behaviour. The runAll harness had to change for the type change; no assertions changed.
